To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attention modification procedure designed to induce attentional engagement with threatening meanings, but not the attention modification procedure that induces selective disengagement, was associated with reduced worry.

attentional engagement with threatening meanings is associated with worry and can be manipulated to produce changes in worry, while attentional disengagement from threatening meanings is not associated with worry and cannot be manipulated to produce change in worry.
When attentional bias was manipulated to facilitate selective engagement with threat meaning, it also gave a rise to a corresponding difference in worry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cognitive processes in the generation and maintenance of anxiety.
understanding the mechanisms that maintain and exacerbate worry.
the role of attention in the development and maintenance of emotional disorders and in particular, the role of attentional bias in worry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attentional bias, in the form of facilitated attentional engagement towards threat, is a causal contributor to worry.
the study provides evidence that attentional bias is a causal contributor to the development and maintenance of worry.
the attentional bias for threat is a necessary but not sufficient condition for worry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attentional engagement with threatening meanings can be induced, and when it does so, it can also induce a corresponding increase in worry.
the more you engage in worry the more you will worry, and the less you engage in worry, the less you will worry.
the more we are able to engage with threat meanings, the more we are likely to worry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of attentional bias in the maintenance of worry may depend on the type of bias induced.
the attentional mechanisms underlying the development of worry can be influenced by experimental manipulations.
attentional bias can be induced in a way that causally influences worry.
